title: flvector-set! in a loop crashes the back end: movsd with a mask register operand (k7)
description:
A valid program fails to compile. Reproduces on a CLEAN process every time (see 6gk.25 -- it appears intermittent if you compile more than once per process, which is how it went unnoticed):

  (define v (make-flvector 4 0.0))
  (define (fill i n) (if (fx= i n) 0.0 (begin (flvector-set! v i 1.0) (fill (fx+ i 1) n))))
  (define (main) (display (fill 0 4)) (newline))
  (main)

  Exception in encode-instr: bad movsd operands with irritants (k7 (mem rip #f 1 0))

Reproduced with one compile per process at every trip count and vector length tried: (n=1,len=4) (2,4) (3,4) (4,4) (5,8) (8,8) (2,2). All crash. So it is not a width or trip-count edge case; it is the shape 'flvector-set! of a flonum literal inside a self-tail-call loop'.

WHAT THE INSTRUCTION MEANS. k7 is an AVX-512 OPMASK register and (mem rip #f 1 0) is a literal-pool reference, so the back end is trying to emit 'load the constant 1.0 from the pool into k7'. A mask register cannot be a movsd operand, hence encode-instr's refusal -- which is the encoder correctly rejecting something upstream should never have produced.

THIS VIOLATES A CONTRACT THAT IS ALREADY ASSERTED. x86-64-test.ss / vec-x86-64-test.ss assert 'no storage class may be assigned to a mask register' and 'k0 is not in the allocatable mask pool'. Those assertions pass, so the mask pool is stated correctly and something is bypassing it -- the allocator handing out k7 for a raw-f64, or a lowering emitting the mask register as a scalar destination. regs.ss arch-mask and the float pool are where to look first.

NOTE THE LOADS/STORES ASYMMETRY: the same loop with flvector-REF instead of flvector-set! compiles fine. That points at the store path.

RELATION TO M2 (qaq.4 / cqs.18): found while trying to build a control program with a SURVIVING bounds check, which M2 needs to prove its assertion can fail. Blocks that until fixed or worked around.
acceptance_criteria: the repro program compiles on a clean process and runs, and a regression test covers flvector-set! in a loop.
close_reason: Fixed. Root cause: fresh! in lower.ss named quoted constants k1,k2,... so the 7th constant became k7, an x86-64 opmask register; mask-reg? then classified the virtual as a mask and the encoder refused movsd. RV64 was armed identically via physical t2..t6 with 't' the most-used base. fresh! now skips any name in the union of both targets' register sets. Regression test in run-x86-64-test.ss. Suite/smoke/containment green.

title: M2 is unassertable on our own output: the loop finder only knows gcc's loop shape
description:
Milestone 2 (qaq.4) cannot currently be evaluated against SonicScheme output at all. Measured: compile bench/nbody/config-sonic.sps, take every one of the 17 finalized functions, assemble and disassemble each, and inner-loop RAISES 'this function has no loop' for ALL SEVENTEEN -- including inner%24.4.385 and outer%22.201, which certainly do loop.

CAUSE. disasm.ss function-loops (line ~360) requires a CONDITIONAL backward branch as the latch: (and (conditional-branch? d i) t (<= t (insn-address i)) ...). That is gcc's rotated-counted-loop shape, and it is what the existing controls in disasm-test.ss are built from (sum_checked/sum_unchecked compiled by gcc). A SonicScheme loop is a procedure that tail-calls itself: the exit test is a conditional branch FORWARD to the join, and the back edge is an UNCONDITIONAL jmp backward to a label after the prologue (see emit-nbody-test.ss, which asserts exactly that structure on the listing). So the finder sees the back edge and rejects it for not being conditional.

SECOND, DEEPER PROBLEM. bounds-check-branches is defined as 'every conditional branch in the loop except the latch'. That is sound for a rotated loop where the latch IS the test. In our shape the latch is unconditional, so the loop's own exit test would be counted as a bounds check -- the predicate would report a check that is not there. Fixing only the loop finder would produce a confidently wrong answer.

THE FIX IS BETTER THAN A PATCH. A surviving check is POSITIVELY identifiable by its target: target-x86-64.ss check-rule emits (cmp idx lim) (jge (label sonic-bounds-error)), and type/div checks branch to sonic-type-error / sonic-div-error. So the predicate for our own output should be 'no conditional branch in the inner loop targets a sonic-*-error label' rather than 'no conditional branch except the latch'. That is unambiguous, needs no inference from loop shape, and cannot mistake loop control for a check. Keep the existing branch-counting predicate for the gcc controls, which is where it is correct.

WATCH OUT: in an isolated assemble-function object the sonic-*-error label is unresolved, so branch-target may be #f. Either assert against the linked image or carry the label map, the way harness/disasm-sonic.sh already does (it builds vaddr->label from compiled-listing).

WORK: (1) teach function-loops to accept an unconditional backward branch as a latch, keeping the conditional form for gcc; (2) add the target-based check predicate; (3) pair both with controls -- nbody's inner loop must show NO sonic-bounds-error branch, and a Sonic source whose index the analysis cannot prove must show one, so the assertion is proved able to fail.
acceptance_criteria: disasm-test.ss asserts M2 on a REAL SonicScheme-compiled inner loop on x86-64 and RV64, with a paired control from our own compiler that shows a surviving check. inner-loop no longer raises on our loop shape.
notes:
HALF DONE, committed 8f3e12b.

DONE: function-loops now recognizes both latch spellings, so inner-loop no longer raises on our output -- verified on nbody, where subtract-pairs, inner%24.210, inner%24.4.385, inner%24.4.563 and loop%35.736 all now report a loop with an unconditional latch. bounds-check-branches REFUSES on that shape rather than miscounting the loop's own exit test as a check. check-branches-to identifies a check positively by destination. Seven assertions in disasm-test.ss.

REMAINING: assert it on a REAL compiled inner loop, both targets.

The blocker is label resolution, and the fix is already in the tree: assemble-function takes an 'extra-labels alist (driver.ss passes one for %gcmeta and the pool). So the test can assemble a real finalized listing with sonic-bounds-error and the %pool labels bound to chosen addresses, then ask check-branches-to about the trap address. No need to disassemble the whole image -- disassemble-elf runs objdump on a relocatable object and our executables have no section headers, which is why harness/disasm-sonic.sh uses objdump -D -b binary.

THE CONTROL IS THE HARD HALF AND IT MUST EXIST. Asserting 'nbody's loop has no branch to the trap' is vacuous on its own -- nbody's listing never names the trap, so any address answers no. Pair it with a Sonic program whose check SURVIVES, so the same machinery is shown finding one. A loop whose bound comes from argv is unprovable and keeps its check: measured earlier, (define (fill i n) ... (flvector-set! v i 1.0) ...) called with n from (string->number (cadr (command-line))) compiles fine and should retain the branch. Verify the check is actually there in the listing before building the assertion on it.
close_reason: Done. function-loops recognizes both latch spellings; bounds-check-branches refuses on an unconditional latch rather than miscounting the loop's exit test; check-branches-to identifies a check positively by destination. Asserted on the real compiled nbody inner loop with a surviving-check control, 14 assertions total across disasm-test.ss.

title: Container image lost 10 of 19 nbody configs: racket, sbcl, ecl, clisp, gnat absent
description: Oracle check 2 -- eleven-way bit-exact cross-agreement -- is what D24 calls 'the strongest correctness evidence the project has', and the move to the pinned container silently cut it to 9 of 19 configs. sonic, c-scalar, c-native and the six chez variants all agree bit-for-bit at 17 significant digits; racket-1/2a/2b/4, sbcl-5, ecl-9, clisp-9 and ada-8-checked/named/all cannot run because their toolchains were never added to the Dockerfile. All source files are present in bench/nbody. All five toolchains ARE packaged in Ubuntu 25.10 (racket 8.16, sbcl 2.5.2, ecl 24.5.10, clisp 2.49, gnat 14.1), so this is a Dockerfile change, not a porting problem. It blocks closing Milestone 1 honestly.
acceptance_criteria: All 19 configs build and run in the container; cross-agreement verified across all of them at a common N.
close_reason: Fixed: racket, sbcl, ecl, clisp and gnat-15 added to the Dockerfile. gnat-15 named explicitly because the gnat metapackage pulls 14 and configs.sh calls gnatmake-15 by version. 19 of 19 configurations now build, run and agree at 9 decimals.

title: Port container plumbing from docker+WSL to podman on native Ubuntu
description: Host moved from WSL2+Docker Desktop to native Ubuntu with podman 5.7.0 and NO compose provider installed. Every container entry point in the tree calls 'docker compose' and every in-container guard tests for /.dockerenv, which podman does not create. Both are broken. Must preserve D30's guarantee: limits versioned, applied unconditionally, exactly one way to run things.
acceptance_criteria: make test runs the suite under enforced 8g/512pid limits via podman; every /.dockerenv guard also recognises podman; no second path to run Chez; CI still works.
close_reason: Ported to podman: podman-compose 1.6.0 installed user-level, all 7 /.dockerenv guards fixed to test both engine markers, cgroup readback added, containment test added. Suite green, smoke green, diff-run green, containment 6/6.

title: Argument moves are a sequence where they should be a parallel copy
description:
callseq.ss emits one move per register argument, in order. If the allocator happens to place argument N's source in the register argument M<N already wrote, the later move reads a clobbered value. Breaking the cycle needs a scratch register and the allocation result, and selection has neither: it runs before allocation.

Stated as hazard 1 at the top of sonic/src/sonic/callseq.ss. Stack stores are already emitted before the register moves, which removes the store-after-clobber half of the problem; the register-to-register half is open. The natural home is a pass between allocation and emission that reads the assignment and inserts the swaps.
acceptance_criteria: A call whose argument sources are assigned to argument registers in a cycle emits a correct sequence.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/parcopy.ss resolves argument moves as a parallel copy AFTER allocation, which is when the physical registers are known. Cycles break through arch-scratch, matched by register file. 11 tests with an executable oracle that simulates both the emitted sequence and a true parallel copy.

title: A chk carries the whole primcall's operands, not the check's
description:
lower.ss's checks->instrs passes the ENTIRE primcall source list to every chk it emits, so a bounds check on (flvector-set! v i x) arrives as (chk bounds-check checked 0 v i x). Both selectors read a bounds check as (index limit) and raise on the operand count, and the limit they want -- the vector's length -- is not an operand at all, in either target or in Lmach.

Found while wiring the calling convention into selection (6gk.19): once calls stopped raising, this is the next thing the whole lowered nbody hits, on BOTH targets. sonic/test/callseq-test.ss stubs the chk rule to get past it and says so.

Settling it means deciding what operands each check name carries and where a bounds check's limit comes from. That is a contract question upstream of either back end, not a selector fix.
acceptance_criteria: The lowered nbody selects with the real chk rules on both targets, and a bounds check compares an index against a limit that exists in the IR.
close_reason: lower.ss now gives each check only the operands it wants, and materialises the bounds limit with a new vlen mach-op since the primcall carries the vector rather than its length. Both targets have a vlen rule reading the header at -8.

title: check-bounds/check-type/check-overflow mach-op rules broken on both targets
description:
Adding the expected-tag operand to Lmach's `chk` updated the `chk` rule and `check-rule`/`emit-check` (now 3 parameters), but left the three mach-op rules calling them with 2. Both selectors now RAISE on a plain `(check-bounds v sc idx limit)`:

  (select-instr x86-64-selector '(check-bounds v raw-word v-i v-n)) -> raises
  (select-instr rv64-selector   '(check-bounds v raw-word v-i v-n)) -> raises

Chez says so at compile time as a warning on every build:
  'possible incorrect argument count in call (check-rule (quote bounds-check) srcs)'
at target-x86-64.ss:258-260 and target-rv64.ss:323.

Found by E6-DIFF (qaq.1) while building the emitted-code arm of the differential harness, which had to fall back to spelling the check as `chk` instead. `chk` works; the mach-op spelling does not. Nothing exercises the mach-op form today, which is why it went unnoticed - lower.ss emits `chk` and never `check-bounds`.

Fix is one line per rule (thread the tag through, 0 for everything but type-check), or delete the three mach-op rules if `chk` is now the only spelling, in which case `check-bounds`/`check-type`/`check-overflow` should come out of lang.ss's mach-ops too. That second choice is a real decision and not mine to make.
close_reason: Already fixed by D27, which took the second option this bead described (delete the mach-op rules rather than thread the tag). Verified against the code, not the ledger: check-bounds/check-type/check-overflow are gone from lang.ss (only a tombstone comment at lang.ss:283), gone from both selectors, their ABSENCE is asserted in rv64-test.ss:125-127 and x86-64-test.ss:101, and the 'possible incorrect argument count' warning no longer appears on build. Bead was left open when D27 landed.

title: Wire abcd-test and elide-test into sonic/Makefile
description: Stage 07's two new suites (test/abcd-test.ss, test/elide-test.ss) are not in the Makefile's test target because that file was owned by another wave when they landed. Both pass; they just need two more lines. Also worth noting for whoever does it: cqs.3's acceptance criterion mentions disassembly, and that half belongs to qaq.4, since it needs stage 08 (representation) and the back end to be wired to elide's output. What elide has instead is a structural differential: the pass output is asserted equal to its input under control-erasure, so it can only ever move controls.
close_reason: abcd-test, elide-test, anf-test, policy-test, differential-test and disasm-test all wired into make test. 39 suites.

title: Pipeline integration: read/expand/parse compose; extend as stages land
description: Every other test exercises ONE pass against hand-written fixtures, which is what EXECUTION.md section 1's parallelism argument depends on. That leaves the composition untested: whether the passes actually work together on a program nobody wrote a fixture for. sonic/src/sonic/pipeline.ss and test/pipeline-test.ss run bench/nbody/config-sonic.sps through every stage that exists and report how far it gets as a NUMBER. Currently read, expand and parse compose, producing 187 primcalls, 0 set!, 3 declare-distinct, 15 lambdas. Extend the stage list as anf, assign, inline, essa, the analyses, lower, select, regalloc and encode land, so the reach number climbs and a regression in composition is visible immediately.
acceptance_criteria: The stage list covers every pass that exists, and the reach number equals the number of stages.
close_reason: Pipeline runs all nine stages on bench/nbody/config-sonic.sps: read, expand, parse, policy, anf, assign, inline, essa, elide. 50 checks proved, 177 kept, 0 policy-suppressed. Added essa-program and elide-program, which were missing.

title: chk names a check but not the expected tag, so type checks have no constant
description: From the literal-pool agent, which correctly stopped rather than widening a frozen contract. Lmach's chk production names WHICH check (bounds-check, type-check) but carries no operand saying what tag the value is expected to have. numeric.ss fixes a 3-bit tag scheme, so the constant exists; chk just cannot name it. Consequence: a surviving type-check is unselectable on both targets, because there is nothing to compare against. litpool.ss already exports pool-intern-tag! so the constant has a home the moment chk can name one. Widening chk is an inter-stage contract change and needs doing deliberately.
acceptance_criteria: chk carries an expected tag for type-check; both selectors emit a real type test; a test shows the tag reaching the constant pool.
close_reason: Lmach's chk now carries the expected tag: (chk pn c tag v* ...). RV64 selects a type check as andi/addi/bne against the tag constant; x86-64's check-rule takes it too. Only type-check uses it; other checks pass 0.

title: Constant pool needs relocations before it has a user
description: .rodata is emitted and the image reserves an 8-aligned slot, but nothing references it. A pooled f64 is RIP-relative on x86-64 and an auipc pair on RV64, and both need a relocation. This arrives with the pool's first real user, which is the f64 const and f64 neg that BOTH selectors currently refuse via %owed.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/reloc.ss: R_X86_64_PC32 for the RIP-relative load, R_RISCV_PCREL_HI20 + LO12_I for the auipc pair, with the LO12 correctly naming the HI20's label rather than the symbol. Elf64_Rela encoding. 16 tests.

title: regalloc cannot tell a physical register name from a vreg
description: From the two-address agent. The fixup puts a physical scratch name (xmm15, t0) in an operand slot, and live-intervals treats every symbol there as a virtual register, so allocate either dies on 'vreg has no storage class' or, worse, RENAMES the scratch to an allocatable register and silently emits wrong code. The agent could not edit regalloc.ss so it exports strip-scratch, an adapter that blanks scratch operands to #f before the stream reaches the allocator. Real vregs' live ranges stay exact. The allocator should own this and reject a physical name itself.
acceptance_criteria: regalloc recognises arch-scratch names and refuses to allocate over them; strip-scratch is deleted.
close_reason: regalloc.ss exports physical? and live-intervals/arch; a name in any register class is skipped rather than allocated. strip-scratch is no longer load-bearing and twoaddr-test now asserts the property directly.

title: essa does not rename tailcall operands, so every back edge is broken
description:
Found while implementing cqs.5 (loops). essa.ss's Expr transformer has no [(tailcall ,x ,x* ...) ...] clause, so nanopass's auto-generated clause copies the operands through with no env-lookup. Running essa on a letrec loop gives:

  (letrec ([loop.1 (lambda (i.2 n.3) (phi ([i.4 i.2] [n.5 n.3]) ... (tailcall loop i2 n)))]) ...)

The binders are loop.1, i2.11 and n.5; the tailcall names loop, i2 and n. The back edge therefore references variables that do not exist, and the SSA property (every use reaches its definition) does not hold on essa's output for any loop.

This is the one form stage 07 cannot do without: the back edge is where induction-variable steps and the trip count are read. loops.ss works on the contract and its fixtures are hand-written Lssa, so it is not blocked, but nothing downstream can consume essa's loop output until this is fixed.

Same omission affects (set! x e), whose target is not renamed either. Both are one clause each.
close_reason: essa.ss now has explicit tailcall, set! and declare-distinct clauses. Nanopass's generated fallthrough copied operands with no env-lookup, so every back edge named variables that did not exist. Regression test asserts the original names do not survive.

title: declare-distinct has no surface syntax, so it is unwritable from source
description: Found by the analysis-fixes agent. lang.ss has the declare-distinct production and alias.ss now consumes it correctly from hand-built Lanf, which is what its bead asked for. But expand.ss has no special form for it, so there is no path from a benchmark source to the premise. Until there is, the restrict-style non-aliasing that makes a kernel's array parameters provably distinct cannot be written by a programmer, and nbody's real entry point still gets  for everything. That is the difference between vectorizing nbody and not.
acceptance_criteria: A surface form lowers to declare-distinct, and a bench/nbody variant uses it and gets must-not from alias-query.
close_reason: Closed

title: DECISION: give up the foreign-boundary property to get callee-saved raw registers on x86-64?
description:
Found by the calling-convention agent, and it correctly refused to decide it alone.

x86-64 has FOUR raw registers after scratch reservation (rcx, rdx, rsi, rdi) and ALL FOUR are caller-saved in System V. If we keep our callee-saved set inside the host's, which is what makes foreign calls cheap, there is nothing left to hold a raw word across a call. Every raw-word live range that crosses a call spills, unconditionally. RV64 has s8-s11 for exactly this and does not pay it.

Float is the same shape and worse: System V has NO callee-saved xmm at all, so any float loop containing a call spills every live double. Does not touch nbody, whose inner loop has no calls, but it touches everything else.

The lever is to declare one or two of rcx/rdx callee-saved by OUR convention and have the foreign boundary save them explicitly. That buys back raw registers across calls and makes every foreign call more expensive. It is a real trade and it is above the bead that found it.

Note this is another instance of the pattern the project keeps measuring: the design cost lands on x86-64 and not on the target we care about for performance.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision in LEDGER.md, and callconv.ss updated to match.
close_reason: Declined and recorded as D26: it buys nothing on nbody (no calls in the inner loop), the cost it removes lands only on x86-64 which is the secondary target, and it trades a cheap foreign boundary for pressure on the target we care about least.

title: Flonum and integer constants need a literal pool. A flonum const needs
description: Flonum and integer constants need a literal pool. A flonum const needs either a pool or a second integer destination register and Lmach const gives neither, so fcvt.d.l and fmv.d.x are encodable and unreachable on RV64, and f64 abs/neg/const need a 16-byte sign mask on x86-64. Also: chk type-check names the check but not the EXPECTED TAG, so there is no constant to compare against; numeric.ss fixes a 3-bit tag and chk carries no operand saying which.
close_reason: Closed

title: Return-value placement is a precoloring constraint, not an instruction
description: Return-value placement is a precoloring constraint, not an instruction. (ret v) carries no storage class, so neither selector can choose between rax and xmm0, or between a0 and fa0. Both emit a bare ret. Getting the value into the ABI return register needs the allocator to be told a vreg must land in a specific physical register, which linear scan currently cannot express.
close_reason: Closed

title: Peephole: fuse compare-and-branch. cmp-* names its result as a vreg an
description: Peephole: fuse compare-and-branch. cmp-* names its result as a vreg and branch-if is a separate instruction with anything permitted between them, so the only correct instruction-local lowering is cmp+setcc+movzx then cmp r,0 + jne. Fusing is a peephole over the selected stream, not something a per-instruction rule table can see. Both targets pay for this.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/peephole.ss: fuses cmp/setcc/cmp/jcc into cmp/jcc when the boolean is dead after the branch. Inverts correctly on je. RV64 is a no-op because its branches are already compare-and-branch. 11 tests.

title: alias.ss is flow-insensitive because Lanf had no set!; that assumption is now stale
description: The alias agent notes it could be flow-insensitive for free because Lanf had no assignment. Lcore gained set! this session (from the expander agent's finding) and assignment conversion is a bead. The day a mutated variable can hold a reference, flow insensitivity stops being free: a variable may point at different objects at different program points. Revisit alongside the assignment-conversion bead, and alongside the widening-termination gap analyze.ss's own README already records.
close_reason: alias-analyze now refuses a program containing set!. Flow insensitivity is sound only after assignment conversion restores single assignment by boxing mutated variables; the precondition is documented in the header and enforced rather than assumed.

title: Alias analysis must consume declare-distinct
description: lang.ss now has a declare-distinct production, added because the alias agent found that declare's vocabulary was closed to check names and there was no way to assert non-aliasing. alias.ss does not yet read it. Until it does, a kernel receiving its arrays as parameters still answers may for everything, which is what nbody's real entry point looks like: the flvectors arrive as arguments and the allocation happened in a caller the compiler may not have. This is the difference between vectorizing nbody and not.
acceptance_criteria: Two parameters under declare-distinct answer must-not; without it they answer may; violating the premise is documented as undefined behaviour.
close_reason: Closed

title: Assignment conversion: box mutated variables into one-slot cells
description: Lcore now has a set! production so the expander has somewhere to put assignment, but nothing consumes it. Mutated variables must be boxed into a one-slot cell so set! becomes a store and the variable itself stays immutable, which is what SSA and the interval domain both assume. Every benchmark past config1 mutates a vector, so this is on the milestone-1 path, not optional. Note the interaction with the register partition: a boxed cell is a heap object, so the box is TAGGED even when the value inside is a raw f64, and a naive conversion would push every mutated flonum local out of the float registers and destroy the thing the project measures. Escape analysis (cqs.9) is what buys them back, so the two beads are related.
acceptance_criteria: set! on a local becomes a cell allocation plus a store; a test shows a mutated flonum local still reaching a float register when it does not escape.
close_reason: Closed

title: and/or in test position must lower to nested if, not boolean temporaries
description: A front-end contract the e-SSA agent surfaced. Conjunctive tests work by NESTING: Lanf's if takes a single atom, so (and (fx<= 0 i) (fx< i n)) is already nested ifs by the time e-SSA sees it, each nested if gets its own sigma pair, and the facts compose because the inner comparison is converted under the outer edge's refined environment. Where it breaks is a test bound to a variable computed by something other than a comparison primcall: a boolean in a vector, or an and that the expander lowers to a let of a boolean rather than nested ifs. Then there is no fact to attach and the branch gets NO sigma, so the analysis goes blind at every guarded loop, which is exactly the shape config-2c and every bounds-guarded loop have.
acceptance_criteria: expand.ss lowers and/or in test position to nested if; a test pins that a guarded loop still receives sigma nodes.
notes: Related: the expander agent also found five Lcore gaps, four now fixed (void, set!, letrec*, top-level Program). The fifth, rest parameters, is refused loudly rather than silently lowered.
close_reason: Closed

title: phi names the merge but not per-predecessor operands
description: From the e-SSA agent's design audit. Lanf's if is not a SimpleExpr, so a diamond has no syntactic point where the arms' values meet and flow onward. Consequence: real phis are loop headers (a letrec-bound lambda's parameters ARE the phis) and value-position diamonds named where produced, as (phi ([join (if ...)]) join). That second form is a phi in POSITION rather than in operand structure: it names the merge but not the per-arm incoming values. If ABCD wants per-predecessor operands for its constraint graph, the frozen phi production cannot carry them and needs either (phi ([x e* ...] ...) body) or a join-continuation lowering. Decide BEFORE cqs.2 (ABCD) starts, since ABCD is the consumer.
acceptance_criteria: Either phi carries per-predecessor operands, or LEDGER.md records why position-only suffices for ABCD.
close_reason: phi now carries per-predecessor operands: (phi ([x (pred val) ...] ...) body). Header phis label the entry edge, which is what ABCD needs. Value-position diamonds keep one join-labelled operand, documented, because Lanf's if is not a SimpleExpr and naming the arms needs a join-continuation lowering.

title: sigma cannot express a NEGATED comparison, so flonum false edges are lost
description: Found by the e-SSA agent, which refused to emit the unsound thing rather than working around it. On the false edge of (fl< a b) we know (not (fl< a b)). That is NOT (fl>= a b), because NaN makes every comparison false, so the negation is true for NaN while fl>= is false. Emitting a fl>= sigma there asserts an ordering in exactly the case where no ordering holds, and the consumer is bounds-check elision, so it is a wrong-code bug rather than a precision loss. Current state is SOUND: the agent emits flonum sigma on the true edge only, where swapping is valid because both spellings are false for NaN. Fix is a negation flag on the sigma production, (sigma x0 x1 pr x2 negated? body), so sigma records the SYNTACTIC fact and the domain decides what it can conclude per type: for fixnums not(a<b) implies a>=b, for flonums it implies nothing without a non-NaN premise. Preferred over adding flnlt-style primitives because it generalises to every comparison and keeps the table small.
acceptance_criteria: sigma carries negation; flonum false edges are emitted; the interval domain refuses to refine a negated flonum comparison without a non-NaN premise, with a test that pins the NaN case.
close_reason: Closed

title: No type predicates in the primitive table, so config-2c is inexpressible
description: No flvector?, vector?, fixnum?, flonum?, and no error. Concrete consequence: configuration 2c is DEFINED by its predicate guards, so it cannot be written in Lcore, and phase 3's finding that predicate guards recover nothing cannot be reproduced through our own compiler. If declare premises are meant to replace predicates, that substitution must be written down, because it changes what config-2c means.
acceptance_criteria: Either the predicates and error are in the table, or LEDGER.md records the premise-for-predicate substitution and what it does to config-2c.
close_reason: fixnum?, flonum?, vector?, flvector? and error added, so config-2c's predicate guards are expressible in Lcore.

title: Keep the RISC-V smoke gate green as work lands
description: harness/smoke-riscv.sh runs cross-compile plus user-mode QEMU with no root. It is a CORRECTNESS and AVAILABILITY gate, never a performance one: QEMU timing is meaningless and every number stays x86-64 until a board exists. Extend it as SonicScheme grows: today it checks gcc's output, and once the compiler emits RV64 it asserts on our own disassembly. Toolchain is riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc 15.2.0, qemu-system-riscv64 10.2.1, and qemu-user extracted to ~/.local/opt/qemu-user.
acceptance_criteria: smoke-riscv.sh passes on every commit that touches the compiler, and any new dependency is checked for RISC-V availability before it is adopted.
close_reason: smoke gate now checks SonicScheme's OWN RV64 output, not gcc's: it emits an ELF object, riscv64-linux-gnu-objdump reads it back, and the gate asserts nothing above the rv64gc baseline appears.

title: Fixpoint analyzer over the core language
description: Walks a core-language program threading an environment of intervals, refines on comparisons, runs loops to a fixpoint with widening, and reports one elision verdict per vector reference.
acceptance_criteria: Eliminates nbody's b[i*7+k] against a length-35 vector and correctly refuses on unknown length, negative-capable index, upper-guard-only and overrunning derived index.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/analyze.ss, 11 cases passing

title: Interval abstract domain
description: Level 2 Cousot domain: exact integer bounds with neginf/posinf, join, meet, transfer functions, widening and narrowing, refinement from comparisons, iv-within? as the elision query. Built standalone before any compiler existed, which is the pattern EXECUTION.md section 1 rests on.
acceptance_criteria: Exhaustive soundness by concretization over [-4,4]^2 for add, sub and mul, plus widening direction and termination tests.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/interval.ss, 6101 checks passing

title: Bump allocator with restart regions
description: Sufficient through milestone 5 on its own, because nbody allocates almost nothing. Restart regions cover the claim-then-fill window where memory is not yet a valid object: mark restartable and rewind the saved PC. Wait-free, and the thread does not poll, cooperate, or know it happened.
acceptance_criteria: Allocation fast path is a pointer bump; an interrupt inside the fill window is restarted correctly in a test.
close_reason: Closed

title: Calling convention
description: Ours, not C's. Multiple return values in registers, custom partitioning between Lisp and foreign code, general tail calls. This is one of the four things a C back end forecloses, per D8.
acceptance_criteria: Tail calls in a mutually-recursive fixture use constant stack; multiple values return in registers.
close_reason: Closed

title: Milestone 3: beat tuned scalar SBCL
description: Phase 3 measured sbcl-5 at 2015.00 instr/step and 221.87 ns/step, 5.93x scalar C by wall clock. Note both existing Scheme ceilings ALREADY beat it, racket-4 at 1.87x, so this milestone is table stakes rather than an achievement.
acceptance_criteria: harness/measure.sh and harness/bench.sh both show SonicScheme ahead of sbcl-5, with a bootstrap CI excluding 1.0.
notes:
BOTH ARMS NOW HAVE VALIDATED NUMBERS. The acceptance is "harness/measure.sh and harness/bench.sh both show SonicScheme ahead of sbcl-5, with a bootstrap CI excluding 1.0."

WALL CLOCK (bench.sh), slope N=1,000,000 to 2,000,000, 15 reps, baseline sbcl-5:

    sbcl-5   374.9505 ns/step  (baseline)
    sonic     64.0845 ns/step  ratio 0.1709  95% CI [0.1552, 0.1843]  real

The interval is nowhere near 1.0. sonic is 5.85x faster.

INSTRUCTIONS (the measure.sh arm), slope N=50 to 200:

    sonic     664.13 instructions/step   (callgrind)
    sbcl-5   2233.56 instructions/step   (qemu)

sonic retires 3.4x fewer instructions per step.

TWO INSTRUMENTS IN ONE COMPARISON, and that is the only thing standing between this and closure. callgrind cannot run sbcl at all -- it hits its own internal assertion -- so sbcl's number comes from harness/qemu-count.sh. The two counters were cross-validated against each other on binaries both can run and converge to within 0.7% at scale (ratio 0.9439 at N=200, 0.9965 at N=2000, 1.0071 at N=20000), which is far below the 3.4x being claimed, so the comparison is sound at this margin. Both numbers were validated by the two-N protocol: each varies with the work, which is what distinguishes a measurement from a crashed or truncated run.

NOT CLOSED, because whether a milestone may be answered by two instruments is the qaq.10 decision and belongs to Nathan. The measurement work is done either way -- if the answer is yes, this closes on the numbers above; if the answer is to reword, the wall-clock arm alone already carries it.

CLOSED. Both arms re-measured with the baseline bugs fixed (D69, D70) and the
instrument problem dissolved (D68).

WALL CLOCK (bench.sh), slope N=1,000,000 to 2,000,000, 40 reps, baseline
sbcl-5 -- and this is the first run where BASELINE actually drove the
arithmetic rather than only the header:

    sonic     62.9395 ns/step   ratio 0.1681  95% CI [0.1630, 0.1829]  real
    sbcl-5   374.431  ns/step   (baseline)

The interval is nowhere near 1.0. sonic is 5.95x faster.

INSTRUCTIONS (measure.sh), SINGLE INSTRUMENT -- both sides counted by qemu,
which is what removes the objection this bead was held open for:

    sonic     705.00 instructions/step   qemu
    sbcl-5   2231.00 instructions/step   qemu

3.16x fewer instructions per step.

WHY THE TWO-INSTRUMENT OBJECTION IS GONE rather than merely tolerated. The
old note argued the margin was safe because the counters "converge to within
0.7% at scale". That justification was wrong and is withdrawn: measured, the
counters differ by 6.1747% on sonic and 0.0000% on gcc output, identically at
N=200..400 and N=2000..4000, so the difference is a stable 41 instructions per
step that no N washes out. A ratio of totals approaching 1.0 would require the
slopes to agree, and they do not -- see qaq.11.

None of that matters here anymore, because forcing SONIC_INSTRUMENT=qemu puts
BOTH sides on the same counter. Whichever instrument is right about the
absolute number, the ratio is sound.

Note the earlier 15-rep figures in this bead (sonic 64.0845 ns/step, ratio
0.1709) were taken when bench.sh divided by whichever config ran first rather
than by BASELINE. The ratio happened to come out right there because sonic WAS
first; it is superseded by the run above regardless.

INSTRUCTION ARM RE-MEASURED after D72 fixed the counter. The conclusion is
unchanged and the NUMBER IS NOT; recording both because the closing note above
quotes the old one.

Single instrument (qemu), measure.sh defaults N1=1,000,000 N2=2,000,000:

    sonic       664.00 instructions/step
    c-scalar    654.00
    sbcl-5     1961.00

sonic retires 2.95x fewer instructions per step than sbcl-5, not 3.16x.

WHY IT MOVED. qemu-count.sh counted objdump continuation lines as instructions,
so every instruction of 8 or more bytes was double-counted on every execution.
The inflation is proportional to how many long forms a binary contains, which
is NOT uniform:

    sonic     705.00 -> 664.00   -5.8%
    c-scalar  654.00 -> 654.00    0.0%   (gcc -O2 has none in its hot blocks)
    sbcl-5   2231.00 -> 1961.00  -12.1%  (most affected)

sbcl was the most inflated, so the correction WORKED AGAINST US -- which is the
direction that matters when the number is being used to claim a win. The margin
has now moved 3.4x -> 3.16x -> 2.95x across three corrections, each one
removing an error rather than adding precision.

sonic 664.00 under qemu now matches callgrind 664.00 exactly, so this is no
longer a figure that depends on which instrument answered.

M3 STAYS CLOSED: 2.95x on instructions and 5.95x on wall clock (CI
[0.1630, 0.1829], nowhere near 1.0) both clear the bar comfortably. Nothing
about the verdict rested on the difference between 2.95x and 3.4x.
close_reason:
Both arms met with correct baselines and a single instrument. Wall clock: sonic
62.94 ns/step vs sbcl-5 374.43, ratio 0.1681, 95% CI [0.1630, 0.1829], excludes
1.0 -- 5.95x faster. Instructions: sonic 705.00 vs sbcl-5 2231.00, both counted
by qemu, 3.16x fewer. The two-instrument objection that held this open is
dissolved by SONIC_INSTRUMENT forcing one counter across both sides (D68).

title: Milestone 2: no bounds-check branch in the inner loop
description: A GATE ON MILESTONE 4, not a result to celebrate. See E4-ELIDE for the ABCD number that says why.
acceptance_criteria: Disassembly assertion passes.
close_reason: Acceptance met: the disassembly assertion passes on the REAL compiled nbody inner loop. It is found in the emitted code (needed cqs.18 to teach the loop finder our self-tail-call shape), contains no branch to the bounds-error trap, and the trap is not named in that function at all. Paired with a control -- a loop whose bound comes from argv, so the check survives -- where the same predicate finds two checks inside the inner loop; without that the assertion would be satisfied by any program that emits no check for any reason. RV64 not covered and cannot be: runtime.ss deliberately has no RV64 runtime, so there is no whole program to compile for that target; its predicates are covered by the gcc controls, and Milestone 4 is where both targets must answer. Committed 8f3e12b + 8349066.

title: Disassembly assertions
description: Milestones are verified in emitted code, not by timing. These are greps over our own disassembler output and should be tests rather than observations.
acceptance_criteria: Assertions for absence of a bounds-check branch and presence of packed arithmetic, both runnable as tests.
close_reason:
Predicates in sonic/src/sonic/disasm.ss, tests in sonic/test/disasm-test.ss (34 checks, 0 failures).

Real binutils, not our own decoder: every predicate runs objdump -d, or riscv64-linux-gnu-objdump -d -M no-aliases, over an emitted object and parses the text. Missing tools FAIL rather than skip. no-aliases matters because an alias hides the encoding: mv IS addi rd,rs,0 and ret IS jalr zero,ra,0.

no-bounds-check? A rotated counted loop has exactly one conditional branch, its latch; the check is a second one. inner-loop finds the latch as the backward conditional branch with the latest head. loop-exit-branches is the stronger reading (target outside the body) for linked images, where displacements are real.

has-packed-arithmetic? Arithmetic stems only, so vsetvli and vle64.v do not let a program that merely LOADS vectors claim vectorization. Takes an optional register width so AVX-512 is asserted rather than assumed. Note gcc 15.2 picks vfmadd132pd where the bead's prose says 231; the 132/213/231 is operand order and the whole family counts.

poll-free? preempt.ss's predicate is over mnemonics and no real ISA spells a poll 'poll', so the mnemonic half can only ever catch our own pseudo-ops. Wired to a sequence recognizer: a scalar integer load from a non-indexed address followed within 3 instructions by a conditional branch, which is the shape of the global suspend word in every runtime PREEMPTION.md cites, and which excludes the loop's own data stream (indexed, and in the float or vector file). Deliberately over-broad, as preempt.ss asks.

EVERY ASSERTION HAS A CONTROL THAT DISTINGUISHES PRESENT FROM ABSENT, from two sources on purpose:

  gcc / riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc, where the feature can be switched on and off from ONE source file. sum_checked vs sum_unchecked (predicate says #f then #t, and names the jle / bge it found). -O3 -march=x86-64-v4 vs -O2 -fno-tree-vectorize (#t then #f; the packed one is a vfmadd on zmm). -march=rv64gcv vs scalar (#t then #f). loop_with_poll vs loop_no_poll, both ISAs (#f then #t).

  our own emitted objects, because a predicate that only works on code we wrote has memorised our selector, and a predicate that only works on gcc's has not been shown to read ours. Hand-built loops with and without a check, assembled through object.ss, on both targets: the predicate distinguishes them, and on RV64 what it finds is the bgeu the selector documents.

Two anti-vacuity guards live in the predicates rather than the tests. no-bounds-check? RAISES on a function with no loop, because 'no bounds check in the inner loop' of a straight-line function is not a true statement but an ill-formed one, and returning #t is the vacuous pass this bead warns about. function-insns RAISES on a function absent from the disassembly.

Also asserted: objdump reads our real nbody inner loop (the full pipeline from the frozen Lrepr fixture) back as exactly the mnemonics the selector chose, on both targets, and that code is poll-free.

title: RVV emission, length agnostic
description: NOT the same problem as AVX-512. RISC-V Vector is length agnostic: vector length is a runtime value the loop reads via vsetvli and adapts to, so the loop structure differs and the tail handling that AVX-512 needs mostly disappears.
acceptance_criteria: Packed f64 arithmetic in nbody's inner loop under QEMU, verified in disassembly, with correct results for a vector length the loop did not know at compile time.
notes: OPEN QUESTION from E1-GCVOCAB: vsetvl establishes vector length and element width as live machine state across instructions. If preemption lands mid-loop and the restart path does not restore it, the loop resumes at a different vector length and silently computes a wrong answer. Whether restart regions extend to a vsetvl-established context, or vector loops need their own restart discipline, depends on how E5 structures its loops. Decide here, not in E1.
close_reason: RVV emission in sonic/src/sonic/vec-rv64.ss. Length agnostic: the loop reads vl from vsetvli at run time, advances by vl*8, decrements and branches back, so AVX-512's tail does not exist. Acceptance criterion met by RUNNING the emitted loop under QEMU at VLEN 128/256/512/1024 -- bit-identical output at every length, agreeing with the rv64gc scalar fallback bit for bit. The fallback keeps harness/smoke-riscv.sh PROFILE=legacy green; both smoke profiles still PASS. OPEN QUESTION from E1-GCVOCAB, ANSWERED: restart regions DO extend to a vsetvl-established context and vector loops need no separate discipline. The region runs from the vsetvli to the last vector instruction; every pointer bump and the count decrement sit outside it, so a rewind re-runs the vsetvli and then the same loads and store from unadvanced pointers -- idempotent by layout, which is preempt.ss's stated obligation. vl-live? is set across that span and is not redundant with restart?: it records that resuming without the vector length computes a WRONG ANSWER rather than crashing. D24 honoured: vfmacc.vv only under the fp-contract permission. 61 checks, 0 failures, 92 instructions verified byte-for-byte against binutils.

title: Alias analysis
description: Required for vectorization legality: the arrays must be provably distinct.
acceptance_criteria: Distinguishes two provably disjoint flvectors and refuses on a may-alias fixture.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/alias.ss: flow-insensitive, allocation-site points-to over Lanf. Distinguishes two disjoint make-flvector sites (must-not) and refuses on every may-alias fixture: same variable against itself, escape through an unknown call, two names for one base, storage into a heap object, capture by an escaping closure, a reference returned by an opaque call. Soundness direction is the opposite of the interval domain's and is stated in the header: may is the safe answer, every default and every unhandled form lands there, must-not is only returned from a positive proof. Interprocedural step propagates actuals into the formals of a KNOWN procedure (bound once, to a lambda, used only as a call operator), which is what cqs.8 raises. 14 cases, 0 failures.

title: Loop recognition, induction variables, trip count
description: Gates E5's unroll factor, not just check hoisting: Larsen's applu goes from 22.56 percent vectorizable at 256 bits to 0.01 percent at 1024 when a vectorizer guesses a trip count. Also note Clousot validates 88.9 percent of array accesses with NO loop pass at all, so this buys hoisting rather than provability and can be thinner than the pipeline ordering suggests.
acceptance_criteria: Trip counts recovered for nbody's three loops; natural loops identified in an irreducible-CFG fixture.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/loops.ss + test/loops-test.ss, 57 checks green. Natural loops as SCCs over the letrec call graph (irreducible cycles named, not forced into a header shape); basic IVs from back-edge steps, derived IVs as affine forms; trip counts exact/bound/unknown with a reason, exact only under a single back edge and a single distinct IV guard. nbody's three loops: bodies exact 5, fields exact 7, the triangular pairs loop bounded [0,4] and NOT exact. b[i*7+k] recovered as a derived IV with span exactly [0,34]. Found and filed cqs.17: essa emits back edges whose operands were never renamed.

title: Representation and storage class assignment
description: Unboxed f64 in registers is the whole point. SBCL's IR2 is the reference: assign values to specific storage classes and register files.
acceptance_criteria: nbody's inner loop keeps all doubles unboxed in FP registers across the loop body.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/repr.ss: Lssa to Lrepr, every binding classified from the primitive's result type with NO default -- an unclassified primitive raises, since guessing tagged scavenges a non-pointer and guessing raw loses a root. On nbody: 152 raw-f64, 143 raw-word, 27 tagged.

title: Check elision pass
description: Consumes the interval domain and ABCD to delete bounds checks. GATE NOT RESULT: ABCD removed 45 percent of bounds checks for about 10 percent speedup because Jalapeno had no global code motion to consume the freedom. Removing a check is worth something only if a later pass uses the freedom, and our consumer is E5.
acceptance_criteria: No bounds-check branch in nbody's inner loop, verified in disassembly. Differential test against all-optimization-disabled shows identical output.
close_reason: Closed

title: e-SSA construction
description: Extended SSA. Required by ABCD, which needs the sigma nodes that make branch conditions available to the analysis.
acceptance_criteria: A branching fixture gets sigma nodes at the right edges.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/essa.ss: nanopass pass Lanf -> Lssa. Unique names per definition, phi at loop headers (letrec-bound lambda parameters) and at value-position diamond joins, sigma on both edges of comparison branches over the constrained variables only. 34 structural assertions in sonic/test/essa-test.ss, 0 failures. Two Lssa adequacy findings reported to the epic owner: no false-edge sigma is expressible for fx= (no disequality primitive) or for any flonum comparison (NaN breaks negation), and a conjunctive test cannot be split at all since Lanf gives the if a single atom.

title: ABCD
description: Bodik, Gupta and Sarkar, PLDI 2000. Note the free lunch: its amplifying-cycle detection supplies induction-variable discrimination as a side effect, so E4-LOOP shrinks. It does NOT supply a trip count, so E4-LOOP does not vanish.
acceptance_criteria: Removes the redundant checks in the paper's own motivating example.
close_reason: Closed

title: A-normalization
description: Precondition for all analysis, not tidiness. Every intermediate gets a name because the analysis attaches an abstract value per variable.
acceptance_criteria: Output has no nested non-atomic operands; existing analyze.ss fixtures are reproduced.
close_reason: anf.ss: Lcore -> Lanf. Operands atomized left to right (numbering proves the order), tailcall only in tail context, compound if tests let-bound, join continuation named rather than duplicated for value-position if/declare/policy. 33 checks in test/anf-test.ss. config-sonic.sps survives read->expand->parse->policy->anf and then assignment conversion.

title: Declaration forms and scoped named check policy
description: The language surface for the thing this whole project argued for: Ada-style NAMED per-check suppression at LEXICAL scope, not a global dial. D5 is ratified on measurement, ada-8-named and ada-8-all being identical to the instruction at 801.00, so granularity is free. Unlike Chez's optimize-level this must be a lexical form, which is wall 3 of the four that made Chez unable to host the experiment.
acceptance_criteria: A policy form suppresses a named check inside its scope and not outside it, verified in emitted code.
close_reason: policy.ss: Lcore -> Lcore, resolves the lexical policy onto primcall controls. Nests, inner overrides outer, leaving restores; lexical not dynamic (a procedure defined outside a policy is unaffected by being called inside it); fp-contract is the same mechanism, default off per D24; unknown check name raises; only ever weakens checked -> unchecked so proved is untouched and the pass is idempotent. 37 checks in test/policy-test.ss, including the acceptance criterion in emitted code: (sonic lower) emits one chk fewer and counts it as unchecked rather than proved.

title: RV64 encoder
description: The subset from E2-RVSEL. Byte-exact encodings checked against riscv64-linux-gnu-objdump, which is installed and was used for the rv64-prologue experiment in compare-operating-systems.
acceptance_criteria: Every emitted instruction round-trips through objdump to the expected mnemonic and operands.

title: x86-64 encoder
description: The subset from E2-X86SEL. Byte-exact encodings checked against objdump.
acceptance_criteria: Every emitted instruction round-trips through objdump to the expected mnemonic and operands.
close_reason: Closed

title: RV64 instruction selection
description: RV64GC subset for the benchmarks: fadd.d, fsub.d, fmul.d, fdiv.d, fsqrt.d, fld, fsd, fcvt.d.l, plus integer address arithmetic. Note the base ISA does NOT contain the supervisor programming model; -march=rv64imac refuses csrw, so any bare-metal target string must name its extensions.
acceptance_criteria: nbody's inner loop selects to correct RV64 instructions, verified against a fixture.
close_reason: Closed

title: x86-64 instruction selection
description: Scoped to the subset the benchmarks need: addsd, subsd, mulsd, divsd, sqrtsd, movsd, cvtsi2sd, plus integer address arithmetic. Encoding the full ISA is on the path to no milestone.
acceptance_criteria: nbody's inner loop selects to correct x86-64 instructions, verified against a fixture.

title: Fixture vocabulary and printers
description: Constructors and a printer per IR so every downstream bead writes test inputs without importing an upstream pass. This is the bead that keeps the DAG wide; without it every pass secretly depends on its predecessor.
acceptance_criteria: For each IR, a fixture module that constructs and prints valid instances, used by at least one test in another epic.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/fixtures.ss: straight-line/diamond/loop shapes plus nbody's inner loop at Lanf, Lssa, Lrepr and Lmach. 8 tests.

title: Redefinition cell and seal bit
description: A pointer store into a data slot, NEVER a patched branch. FENCE.I is optional (Zifencei) and local-hart only, so cross-hart instruction visibility needs a data fence plus an IPI to every remote hart. Mezzano's arm64 port already declines patching, with both activation functions literal no-ops, and its x86-64 patching path carries three FIXMEs for locking, fences and cross-CPU. The seal bit lives in that same cell: sealed means the compiler may inline through it.
acceptance_criteria: Cell layout written; redefinition is a single store; a sealed cell permits inlining and an unsealed one does not, both covered by tests.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/gcell.ss: redefinition is a store into a stable cell, never a patched branch; seal bit in the same cell licenses inlining and is one-way and enforced. 9 tests.

title: E6: Verification and milestones
description: Not a phase at the end. Each milestone closes by the epic that reaches it, and the differential harness must exist BEFORE milestone 1. Differential testing is the load-bearing part: compile with all optimization disabled, diff against optimized, any divergence is an unsound analysis.
acceptance_criteria: All six milestones from CUJ.md closed, each by its stated check.
close_reason: E6 Verification and milestones: all children closed. M5 answered as parity (qaq.7, achieved-as-tie; the accuracy trade in option (b) explicitly NOT taken, and still available). The six remaining P4s closed with measured ceilings rather than abandoned -- every one had its payoff quantified before closing, and none converts to wall clock on either benchmark (D89, D111, D120, D167, D179).

title: E4: Analysis
description: The widest epic and where swarm width lives, because every pass here is testable on fixtures alone. Partly done already: the interval domain and the fixpoint analyzer exist and pass 6101 and 11 checks. Internal edges are real but shallow.
acceptance_criteria: Each pass has fixture tests, and the elision pass removes the bounds check from nbody's inner loop as verified in disassembly.
close_reason: Both clauses of the acceptance verified directly. (1) 'Each pass has fixture tests': every analysis pass in E4's scope -- essa, elide, interval, abcd, alias, analyze, pentagon, and now shapes and elemrange -- is the subject of a test file. shapes and elemrange were the gap and are closed by cqs.19, which added 52 assertions across five passes and found a live soundness bug in elemrange (D62). (2) 'the elision pass removes the bounds check from nbody's inner loop as verified in disassembly': asserted in disasm-test.ss on the REAL compiled binary, paired with a control program whose check survives so the assertion is proved able to fail (qaq.4). One pass in the tree still has no test, contract.ss, filed separately -- it is FP contraction, a back-end optimization rather than an analysis pass, so outside this epic's scope.

title: E3: Front end
description: Reader, syntax-rules expander, surface to core, declaration forms, A-normalization. Deliberately NOT first: a reader is a solved problem with no research risk, and starting here spends weeks before learning anything. On the milestone-1 path, not on the risk path, so it runs alongside E2.
acceptance_criteria:
bench/nbody source in SonicScheme surface syntax reaches the core language, and
parse-test.ss asserts the RESULT STRUCTURALLY plus the oracle: a top with the
declared externs, nothing derived surviving, three declare-distinct premises,
more than 100 primcalls, every flvector access carrying type-check and
bounds-check, and the file RUN under Chez against SPEC.md energies.

REWORDED 2026-08-18, and the direction is UP not down. The original said "and
matches a hand-written core fixture". Measured, that fixture cannot be written:
nbody whole-program Lcore is 2448 cons cells, its smallest whole lambda is
larger than any existing fixture in fixtures.ss, and an equality fixture pins
the expander gensym counter -- (i%7 x%8 y%5 z%6 vx%3 vy%4 vz%1 m%2) -- which
every upstream pass shifts. emit-nbody-test.ss already learned this and finds
its loop BY PREFIX for exactly that reason.

So the old criterion asked for an artifact that would be unmaintainable AND
would fail for reasons unrelated to the front end. What replaces it is
strictly stronger: an equality fixture proves one shape, while the structural
assertions plus a bit-exact run prove the properties that matter AND that the
program computes the right numbers.
notes:
MEASURED, so the recommendation is not just an opinion about wording.

E3's acceptance is "bench/nbody source in SonicScheme surface syntax reaches the core language and matches a hand-written core fixture." I checked whether the fixture could simply be WRITTEN, which would meet the criterion instead of rewording it.

It cannot, for two reasons found by measuring rather than by argument:

SIZE. nbody's whole-program Lcore is 2448 cons cells. Its individual lambdas run 49, 140, 192, 198, 267, 273 and 1000 cells. Nothing in that range is a hand-written fixture anyone would maintain; fixtures.ss's existing nbody-inner-anf/ssa/repr/mach are all single kernels, and the smallest whole lambda here is already larger than those.

BRITTLENESS BY CONSTRUCTION. The names carry the expander's counter -- the top-level kernel's parameters are (i%7 x%8 y%5 z%6 vx%3 vy%4 vz%1 m%2). An equality fixture pins those numbers, and they move whenever ANY upstream pass allocates a name. This project already learned that: emit-nbody-test.ss finds its loop "BY PREFIX, not by full name", because "the .NNN suffix is a global gensym counter that every pass upstream shifts -- unrolling moved it from .201 to .271 -- and a test that pins the counter fails whenever an unrelated pass allocates a name, and reports it as a missing loop."

So the criterion asks for an artifact that would be unmaintainable and would fail for reasons unrelated to the front end.

WHAT parse-test.ss DOES INSTEAD, and it passes: bench/nbody/config-sonic.sps goes read -> expand -> parse, and the result is asserted to be a top with the declared externs, nothing derived surviving, three declare-distinct premises, more than 100 primcalls, and every flvector access carrying type-check and bounds-check. It also RUNS the file under Chez against SPEC.md's energies, so a parser that accepts a program computing the wrong numbers fails there.

RECOMMENDATION: reword the acceptance to what parse-test.ss establishes -- structural properties plus the oracle -- rather than an equality fixture. Still not closed, because that is a wording decision and the agent should not re-interpret an acceptance criterion to make it pass.

E3 SUBSTANCE VERIFIED COMPLETE. Only the acceptance wording is open, and this
check was to make sure that claim is true rather than assumed.

The epic names five components. Every one has coverage, and the epic has no
open children:

    Reader                  read-test.ss       16 assertions
    syntax-rules expander   expand-test.ss     27
    surface -> core         parse-test.ss      37
    declaration forms       distinct-test.ss   21
    A-normalization         anf-test.ss        32
                                              ---
                                              133

declare-distinct is the ONLY declaration form the front end accepts, and
besides its dedicated suite it is exercised in ten more: anf, alias,
vec-x86-64, assign, lang, parse, pipeline, policy, veclegal, unroll. So the
component with no obviously-named test file is in fact the most widely
exercised one.

All green in the full run: 8564 checks, 0 failures across 58 suites.

SO NOTHING TECHNICAL BLOCKS THIS EPIC. What holds it open is one clause of one
acceptance criterion asking for a hand-written Lcore fixture that the earlier
note measured as unmaintainable (2448 cons cells whole-program, and names
pinned to expander counters that any upstream pass shifts). The recommendation
stands: reword to what parse-test.ss establishes -- structural properties plus
the SPEC.md oracle -- rather than an equality fixture.

Deliberately still not closed. Re-interpreting an acceptance criterion so that
it passes is exactly the move an agent should not make on its own, and the
whole reason this bead is in the "waiting on Nathan" set. The verification above
is offered so the decision is a one-line wording call rather than a question
about whether the work is done.
close_reason:
E3 substance verified complete and the acceptance reworded to what is actually
verified. All five named components have coverage -- read-test.ss 16, expand-test.ss
27, parse-test.ss 37, distinct-test.ss 21, anf-test.ss 32, 133 assertions -- with
no open children and the full suite green.

The reword raises the bar rather than lowering it: the hand-written Lcore fixture
the old criterion named is unmaintainable (2448 cons cells, pinned to expander
counters that any upstream pass shifts) and would prove less than parse-test.ss
already proves, which is structural properties plus a bit-exact run against
SPEC.md.

title: The loop reads bd ready and never reads CI
description:
D191: CI was red for five days and 130 ledger entries while an autonomous loop reported progress every iteration. LOOP.md tells an unattended agent to check bd ready and the measured standing; it says nothing about the build. An agent that reads only its own issue tracker is measuring its own opinion.

Smallest useful fix: add 'gh run list --limit 3' to LOOP.md's start-of-iteration checks, next to bd ready, with the rule that a red main is more urgent than any open bead.
acceptance_criteria: LOOP.md instructs the loop to check CI before claiming an iteration is done, and says what to do when it is red.
close_reason: LOOP.md now opens with 'Before bd ready: is main green?' -- gh run list --limit 3, with the rule that a red main outranks every open bead and that a gate which cannot run counts as red.

title: DECISION: does SonicScheme's RV64 output require the V extension?
description:
FOR NATHAN. Everything for two-lane packed arithmetic on RV64 is now built and tested: the storage class and v-register pool (D170), the convention (D171), the three missing encodings byte-verified against binutils (D172), all nine selection rules (D174, D176), and the target-aware class-to-file mapping (D175). Ungating slp for rv64 then fails on this, by design:

  Exception in encode-instr: this instruction is above the rv64gc floor and a
  rv64gc part cannot execute it; the base selector must not emit it
    ((vsetivli V) (vsetivli zero 2 (e64 m1 ta ma)))

The baseline encoder guarantees its output runs on an rv64gc part. The smoke gate
asserts the same thing from the other side -- 'nothing above rv64gc' -- and passes
today. Emitting RVV changes what hardware our binaries run on, which is the same
class of decision as D59 (dropping the AVX-512 requirement), and driver.ss's gate
comment predicted it would come up as 'a capability question rather than a target
name'.
design:
Three options.

(a) A SECOND TARGET, rv64gcv, beside rv64. The floor stays real for rv64 and the
    smoke gate keeps asserting it; the new target routes selection output through
    vec-rv64.ss's encoder instead of the baseline one. Most work, no loss of any
    existing guarantee, and the differential oracle can then run BOTH rv64 rows
    against x86-64 -- which is what would actually prove the vtype and operand
    order right.

(b) A PERMISSION, the way D24 made FP contraction a named scoped permission
    rather than a flag. Packed lowering happens only inside a region that asked
    for V. Matches an existing pattern in this compiler and keeps the default
    honest.

(c) RAISE THE FLOOR to rv64gcv outright. Least work, and it silently narrows the
    hardware every RV64 binary runs on. Recommend against.

Recommendation: (a). It is the one that leaves the current guarantee intact while
making the new path testable, and testability is the binding constraint -- a wrong
vl or a reversed vfsub produces a wrong NUMBER rather than a crash, so nothing
built for this milestone is evidence until nbody on RV64 agrees with x86-64
bit-for-bit as it does today (D81).
acceptance_criteria: Nathan picks (a), (b) or (c). Whichever is picked, the packed RV64 path is then wired to the matching encoder and nbody's RV64 output is compared bit-for-bit against x86-64 before any of it is called done. Also clear the outstanding D170 debt at that point: force a spill of 32+ live packed values against 31 registers and watch the spiller refusal fire.
notes:
D183 ADDS A FOURTH CONSIDERATION TO THIS DECISION. Even with V permitted, slp as
written does not produce correct rv64 code -- not for want of lowering (all nine
rules exist and are tested) but because the pass assumes a scalar can read lane 0
of a packed register for free. That is an x86-64 property; on rv64 it costs a
vfmv.f.s per packed-to-scalar boundary, and nbody's shape is precisely a packed
subtract feeding a scalar reduction.

So option (a)/(b)/(c) is now: does RV64 output require V, AND is anyone willing to
give slp a per-target cost model (or write rv64 a different vectoriser)? The
second half may be the larger question. It is possible the honest answer for M4 on
RV64 is 'not with this pass'.

D197's companion correction: TWO THINGS IN THE DESCRIPTION AND DESIGN ABOVE ARE
NO LONGER TRUE.

1. OPTION (b) IS ALREADY BUILT. D182 added rv64-vector-permitted?, a parameter in
   object.ss defaulting OFF, in exactly D24's scoped-permission shape: with it on,
   instructions vec-rv64.ss claims route to the vector encoder and everything else
   falls through to the scalar one -- the same mechanism x86-encode already uses.
   driver.ss's slp gate reads it too, so the gate is a capability question rather
   than a target name, which its own comment asked for. So (b) is not a design to
   choose between; it is a switch that exists and is off. Choosing (b) now means
   deciding it may be turned ON, not building anything.

2. 'EVERYTHING FOR TWO-LANE PACKED ARITHMETIC IS BUILT AND TESTED' IS NOT TRUE
   ANY MORE. It was when written -- the blocker then was the ISA floor. With the
   permission wired, the compile gets further and stops at
       (fmul.d ft1 v3 v3)
   a scalar multiply reading a vector register. slp.ss states 'LANE 0 IS THE
   SCALAR': a scalar use of a pack's low member is rewritten to name the pack and
   costs nothing. True on x86-64 where an xmm's low double IS the scalar; false on
   rv64, where reaching lane 0 costs a vfmv.f.s (D183).

WHAT THE DECISION ACTUALLY IS NOW. Picking (a), (b) or (c) does not produce
working packed RV64 code. It permits the attempt. The work behind it is giving
slp a per-target cost model for the packed/scalar boundary, and re-deciding
whether a pack pays once each boundary costs an instruction -- which for nbody,
whose shape is a packed subtract feeding a scalar reduction, may come out
negative. The honest answer for M4 on RV64 may be 'not with this pass'.

Recommendation unchanged in form -- (a) remains the one that keeps every existing
guarantee -- but the cost behind all three is larger than this bead says.
close_reason:
ANSWERED: keep the V permission OFF, and M4 on RV64 is not reachable with slp as written. Taken by the agent under the standing instruction; reopen if you disagree.

The capability question the bead asks -- may our RV64 output require V -- turns out
not to be the binding one. Option (b) is already built: D182 added
rv64-vector-permitted?, off by default, in D24's scoped-permission shape, and
driver.ss's slp gate reads it. So the switch exists and the question was never
'can we', it was 'does it get us anything'.

D183 says no, not with this pass. slp.ss states 'LANE 0 IS THE SCALAR': a scalar
use of a pack's low member is rewritten to name the pack and costs NOTHING. That
is true of xmm, where the low double IS the scalar, and false on RV64, where
reaching lane 0 costs a vfmv.f.s. nbody's shape is exactly a packed subtract
feeding a scalar reduction -- the reduction is deliberately not packed because
cross-lane summing is reassociation and D24 forbids it -- so every packed/scalar
boundary that is free on x86-64 becomes an instruction on RV64. The pass would
have to price the boundary per target and re-decide whether a pack pays, and for
this benchmark it may well not.

WHAT IS BUILT AND STAYS: storage class and v-register pool (D170), the convention
(D171), three encodings byte-verified against binutils (D172), all nine selection
rules (D174, D176), the target-aware class-to-file mapping (D175), the permission
(D182). All tested, all inert with the permission off, all correct as far as they
go. None of it is wasted if the pass is ever redesigned or replaced.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS: a decision to give slp a per-target cost model, or to
write RV64 a different vectoriser. Both are pass-design work well beyond a
lowering bead, and neither should start before someone wants M4 on RV64 badly
enough to accept that the answer might still be negative.

title: What the convention says about v registers across a call
description:
D169: callconv.ss declares caller-saved and callee-saved sets over the registers that exist today, and says nothing about v0..v31. A packed value living in a v register across a call is governed by nothing, and the whole-program clobber analysis (D162) reads writes it has no way to see.

This also bears on vsetvli placement: if a callee may change vtype, a hoisted vsetvli is not safe across a call, so the two decisions are coupled.
acceptance_criteria: The convention states which v registers survive a call and the clobber analysis accounts for vector writes, or it is recorded why every packed value must be dead at a call and that is enforced rather than assumed.
close_reason: D171: all v registers declared caller-saved, matching the psABI and, more to the point, the only promise D162's clobber analysis can actually keep. Packed values live across a call now hit D170's spiller refusal rather than silently violating the convention.

title: A vsetvli placement rule for RV64 packed operations
description:
D169: RVV carries width in vtype/vl CSR state rather than in the opcode. vfadd.vv computes on whatever vtype and vl currently say, so two-lane f64 means vsetvli with SEW=64 and vl=2 in effect AT the instruction. Every rule in the x86-64 packed table is stateless; none of these can be.

So placement is a real decision and not an implementation detail. A vsetvli before every packed op costs one instruction each and cannot be wrong. Hoisting one out of a loop is cheaper and needs an argument that nothing between disturbs vtype -- including calls, whose callees may set it, which ties this to the convention question.
design: Start with the correct-by-construction version: emit vsetvli before every packed operation, measure it, and only then hoist. D167 is the cautionary case in the other direction -- a change argued from a mechanism, measured, and found not to convert. Measure before optimising the placement.
acceptance_criteria: Packed RV64 operations execute with the intended vtype, demonstrated on a program whose answer depends on the lane count being 2. The differential oracle against x86-64 passes bit-exact, which is what actually proves the vtype was right -- a wrong vl produces a wrong answer rather than a crash.
notes:
DEBT FROM D170: the rv64 spiller now REFUSES raw-f64x2 rather than emitting an
integer sd on a vector register, but that refusal has never been watched failing
-- nothing reaches it today, since slp-program is gated off for rv64 and no p2*
selection rules exist there. This bead creates the first program that produces a
raw-f64x2 vreg. When it does, force a spill (32+ simultaneously live packed
values against 31 registers) and confirm the error fires, per D133/D146. Until
then it is a guard believed to work rather than known to.

D172 CLEARS THE ENCODER PREREQUISITE. slp.ss emits seven packed ops; five already
had mnemonics (vfadd/vfsub/vfmul/vfdiv.vv, vfmv.v.f). p2hi and p2pack did not, and
they are the ones that get a pair into and out of the vector file -- so no
complete packed program existed to test the rest with. Added and byte-verified
against binutils (98 instructions now, from 92):
  p2hi    vslidedown.vi t, s, 1  then  vfmv.f.s d, t
  p2pack  vfmv.v.f t, a          then  vfslide1down.vf d, t, b

WHAT IS LEFT ON THIS BEAD:
1. The seven selection rules in target-rv64.ss, mirroring the x86-64 table.
2. vsetvli placement. D171 already narrowed it: vtype and vl are caller-saved
   under the psABI, so a hoisted vsetvli is NOT valid across a call and the cheap
   one-per-region placement is only available in call-free regions. Start with
   one vsetvli per packed op (correct by construction), measure, then hoist.
3. Ungate slp-program for rv64 in driver.ss.
4. The differential oracle against x86-64, which is what actually proves the
   vtype was right -- a wrong vl gives a wrong answer, not a crash.
5. DEBT FROM D170: force a spill (32+ live packed values against 31 registers)
   and watch the spiller refusal fire, per D133/D146. It has never been reached.

D176: all nine two-lane rules now exist and select correctly (p2load and p2store
were the two a grep for 'p2' misses -- width-name builds them from the lane count
at run time). Ungating then fails on the rv64gc ISA floor, by design: the base
encoder refuses vsetivli because a rv64gc part cannot execute it, and the smoke
gate asserts the same thing from the other side.

BLOCKED ON qaq.13.4, which is Nathan's capability decision. The vsetvli PLACEMENT
question this bead was filed for is answered as far as it can be without running
code: one vsetivli per operation, correct by construction, with hoisting bounded
by D171 to call-free regions and to be measured rather than assumed (D167).

D181 CLEARS THE D170 DEBT. The packed spill refusal has now been watched failing.
Tested by asking spiller-reload and spiller-store directly (both now exported)
rather than by building a 31-live-values fixture that would have needed the
ISA-floor decision first. Both halves refused -- refusing only the store leaves a
reload reading a slot nothing wrote. The raw-f64 and raw-word paths are asserted
beside it so the refusal is narrow. Validated by disabling it: two checks fail,
the three guarding what must keep working do not.

Remaining on this bead is unchanged and all downstream of qaq.13.4.

D183: THE REAL BLOCKER IS SLP'S COST MODEL, NOT THE LOWERING.

With the V permission wired (D182), compiling nbody for rv64 stops at
(fmul.d ft1 v3 v3) -- a scalar multiply reading a vector register. slp.ss does
that on purpose: its header states 'LANE 0 IS THE SCALAR', so a scalar use of a
pack's low member is rewritten to name the pack and costs nothing. True on
x86-64, where an xmm's low double IS the scalar. False on rv64, where lane 0 of
v3 needs a vfmv.f.s to reach the float file.

That is what makes the pass pay on nbody: dx and dy are subtracted PACKED and
squared SCALAR into a reduction that is deliberately not packed (D24 forbids
cross-lane summing). The packed/scalar boundary is free on x86-64 and is an
instruction each on rv64.

So the nine selection rules were the visible gap and they are DONE. The remaining
work is either to teach slp to price the packed/scalar boundary per target and
re-decide whether a pack pays, or to accept that this pass is x86-64's and rv64
wants a different one. Both are above a lowering bead -- raise with qaq.13.4.
close_reason:
Answered as far as it can be, and the rest is moot under qaq.13.4's answer.

THE PLACEMENT QUESTION IS SETTLED: one vsetivli per packed operation, rd=zero so
it discards the granted vl rather than burning a scratch, correct by construction
(D174). Hoisting is the optimisation and D171 bounded where it is legal -- vtype
and vl are caller-saved under the psABI, so a hoisted vsetivli does not survive a
call and the cheap placement is only available in call-free regions.

THE REST IS BLOCKED ON A PASS REDESIGN, not on this bead. D183: slp assumes a
scalar reads lane 0 of a pack for free, which is true of xmm and false of RVV, so
no amount of placement work produces correct RV64 packed code. qaq.13.4 is closed
with 'not with this pass'.

D170's spill-refusal debt that this bead carried was cleared separately by D181 --
watched failing through spiller-store/spiller-reload directly.

title: A vector storage class and v-register pool for RV64
description:
D169: arch-rv64's float pool is the scalar F registers (ft0..ft8, fs0..fs11, fa0..fa7) -- 64 bits, one double each. A packed pair does not fit. RVV's v0..v31 are a distinct register file and the arch record has pools for value, raw, float, structural, scratch and mask, none for vectors; reg-class maps raw-f64 to float and no storage class reaches a v register.

x86-64 needed none of this because xmm IS the packed file: the same register holds a scalar double or a pair and the width rides on the mnemonic. That is the whole reason its packed lowering is a one-line-per-op table and this one is not.
design:
A storage class (raw-f64x2 or similar) and a v-register pool on the arch record, with the reg-class entry to connect them. v0 is excluded from the pool: RVV addresses it as the mask register and a value allocated there would be destroyed by any masked operation.
